**A Lesson in Resilience: FFIEC Final Authentication Guidance and Me**

Early in my career, I was part of a team tasked with implementing FFIEC's final authentication guidance for a large financial institution. We were ambitious, thinking we could roll out the new controls in just a few months. But the reality was far from it. As we struggled to meet the compliance deadline, I watched our team's morale plummet. I was frustrated, and I wasn't alone.

The turning point came when our team lead asked us to walk a mile in the customer's shoes. She encouraged us to imagine being a customer trying to log in to their online banking account, only to be stuck in a never-ending loop of password resets and one-time passwords. That moment of empathy helped us understand that the authentication guidance wasn't just about meeting a regulatory requirement, but about protecting our customers' sensitive information.

I learned that sometimes, it's not about being agile, but about being resilient. It's about acknowledging the challenges and being willing to adapt. Today, when I work with teams implementing new controls, I remind them that it's not just about ticking boxes, but about creating a culture of customer-centricity and continuous improvement. What lessons have you learned from implementing complex regulations? How did you navigate the challenges and come out stronger on the other side?
